reading.title: Text 1
reading.en_title: Among the annoying challenges facing the middle class is one that will…
reading.cn_title: 自动化对中产阶层就业的冲击及政策应对
reading.topic: 自动化对中产阶层就业的冲击及政策应对
reading.intro: 本篇主题：自动化对中产阶层就业的冲击及政策应对。先读题干，圈出关键词；回原文找证据句，再用主体、范围、方向排除。

paragraphs.en: Among the annoying challenges facing the middle class is one that will probably go unmentioned in the next presidential campaign: What happens when the robots come for their jobs?
paragraphs.zh: 中产阶层面临着种种恼人的挑战，其中有一个很可能不会在下一届总统竞选中被提及：当机器人来抢他们的工作时，会发生什么？

paragraphs.en: Don’t dismiss that possibility entirely. About half of U.S. jobs are at high risk of being automated, according to a University of Oxford study, with the middle class disproportionately squeezed. Lower-income jobs like gardening or day care don’t appeal to robots. But many middle-class occupations – trucking, financial advice, software engineering – have aroused their interest, or soon will. The rich own the robots, so they will be fine.
paragraphs.zh: 不要完全排除这种可能性。 牛津大学的一项研究显示，美国约有一半的工作面临被自动化取代的高风险，而中产阶层受到的挤压尤其严重。 园艺、日托之类的低收入工作对机器人并没有吸引力。 但许多中产阶层从事的职业——货运、财务咨询、软件工程——已经引起了机器人的“兴趣”，即使现在还没有，也很快会如此。 富人拥有机器人，因此他们不会受到什么影响。

paragraphs.en: This isn’t to be alarmist. Optimists point out that technological upheaval has benefited workers in the past. The Industrial Revolution didn’t go so well for Luddites whose jobs were displaced by mechanized looms, but it eventually raised living standards and created more jobs than it destroyed. Likewise, automation should eventually boost productivity, stimulate demand by driving down prices, and free workers from hard, boring work. But in the medium term, middle-class workers may need a lot of help adjusting.
paragraphs.zh: 这样说并不是要危言耸听。 乐观者指出，过去的技术巨变曾让劳动者受益。 工业革命对卢德派工人而言并不顺利，他们的工作被机械织布机取代；但工业革命最终提高了生活水平，而且创造的工作岗位比摧毁的更多。 同样，自动化最终应当能够提高生产率、通过压低价格来刺激需求，并把劳动者从艰苦乏味的工作中解放出来。 但从中期来看，中产阶层劳动者可能需要大量帮助才能适应这一变化。

paragraphs.en: The first step, as Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee argue in The Second Machine Age, should be rethinking education and job training. Curriculums – from grammar school to college – should evolve to focus less on memorizing facts and more on creativity and complex communication. Vocational schools should do a better job of fostering problem-solving skills and helping students work alongside robots. Online education can supplement the traditional kind. It could make extra training and instruction affordable. Professionals trying to acquire new skills will be able to do so without going into debt.
paragraphs.zh: 正如埃里克·布莱恩约尔松和安德鲁·麦卡菲在《第二次机器革命》中所主张的，第一步应当是重新思考教育与职业培训。 从小学到大学，课程都应当逐步调整，减少对事实记忆的关注，更多培养创造力和复杂沟通能力。 职业学校应当更好地培养学生解决问题的能力，并帮助他们学会与机器人协同工作。 在线教育可以补充传统教育。 在线教育可以让额外培训和教学变得负担得起。 希望掌握新技能的专业人士将能够在不负债的情况下接受这类培训。

paragraphs.en: The challenge of coping with automation underlines the need for the U.S. to revive its fading business dynamism: Starting new companies must be made easier. In previous eras of drastic technological change, entrepreneurs smoothed the transition by dreaming up ways to combine labor and machines. The best uses of 3D printers and virtual reality haven’t been invented yet. The U.S. needs the new companies that will invent them.
paragraphs.zh: 应对自动化的挑战凸显出美国重振其日渐衰退的商业活力的必要性：必须降低创办新公司的难度。 在以往技术发生剧烈变革的时代，企业家通过构想把人力与机器结合起来的新方法，使转型过程更加平稳。 3D 打印机和虚拟现实最理想的用途尚未被开发出来。 美国需要由新公司来开发这些最佳用途。

paragraphs.en: Finally, because automation threatens to widen the gap between capital income and labor income, taxes and the safety net will have to be rethought. Taxes on low-wage labor need to be cut, and wage subsidies such as the earned income tax credit should be expanded: This would boost incomes, encourage work, reward companies for job creation, and reduce inequality.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，由于自动化可能扩大资本收入与劳动收入之间的差距，税收制度和社会保障体系都必须重新设计。 应当降低针对低工资劳动的税负，并扩大劳动所得税抵免等工资补贴：这样做既能提高收入、鼓励就业，也能奖励创造岗位的企业并缩小不平等。

paragraphs.en: Technology will improve society in ways big and small over the next few years, yet this will be little comfort to those who find their lives and careers upended by automation. Destroying the machines that are coming for our jobs would be nuts. But policies to help workers adapt will be indispensable.
paragraphs.zh: 未来几年，技术会从大大小小的方面改善社会；然而，对那些发现自己的生活和职业被自动化彻底打乱的人来说，这并不能带来多少安慰。 摧毁那些正要抢走我们工作的机器，无疑是疯狂之举。 但是，帮助劳动者适应这种变化的政策将不可或缺。

questions.stem: Who will be most threatened by automation?
questions.explain:
正确项：Middle-class workers. 原文明确说中产阶层受到的挤压尤其严重，并列举货运、财务咨询、软件工程等中产职业已经或即将成为自动化的目标，因此受威胁最大的是中产阶层劳动者。
其他选项：A. Leading politicians.：首段只说这一问题可能不会在总统竞选中被提及，并未说主要政治人物的工作会受自动化威胁，属于张冠李戴。；B. Low-wage laborers.：原文说园艺、日托等低收入工作对机器人“没有吸引力”，与该项相反。；C. Robot owners.：原文说富人拥有机器人，因此会安然无恙；机器人所有者是受益或较少受损的一方。
questions.evidence:
About half of U.S. jobs are at high risk of being automated, according to a University of Oxford study, with the middle class disproportionately squeezed.
But many middle-class occupations – trucking, financial advice, software engineering – have aroused their interest, or soon will.

questions.stem: Which of the following best represents the author’s view?
options: Worries about automation are in fact groundless.
Optimists’ opinions on new tech find little support.
Issues arising from automation need to be tackled.
Negative consequences of new tech can be avoided.
questions.explain:
正确项：Issues arising from automation need to be tackled. 作者承认自动化具有长期收益，但全文主体连续提出教育培训、创业环境、税收与社会保障等对策，结尾又强调帮助劳动者适应的政策不可或缺。这表明自动化带来的问题必须得到处理。
其他选项：A. Worries about automation are in fact groundless.：作者用研究数据说明大量岗位确有被自动化的风险，并未认为担忧毫无根据，与原文相反。；B. Optimists’ opinions on new tech find little support.：作者引用工业革命和生产率提升来承认乐观者观点的合理部分，并非说其缺乏支持。；D. Negative consequences of new tech can be avoided.：文章主张帮助劳动者适应并减轻冲击，没有断言所有负面后果都能避免；can be avoided 过于绝对。
questions.evidence: But policies to help workers adapt will be indispensable.

questions.stem: Education in the age of automation should put more emphasis on
questions.explain:
正确项：creative potential. 原文主张课程应减少事实记忆，更多关注 creativity 和复杂沟通能力；creative potential 是对 creativity 的准确同义改写。
其他选项：B. job-hunting skills.：原文谈的是创造力、解决问题和人机协作能力，并未谈求职技巧，属于无中生有。；C. individual needs.：文章讨论面向自动化时代的课程重点，没有提出根据个人需要定制教育，属于偷换概念。；D. cooperative spirit.：work alongside robots 指与机器协同工作的能力，不等同于培养人与人之间的合作精神；且核心定位词是 creativity。
questions.evidence: Curriculums – from grammar school to college – should evolve to focus less on memorizing facts and more on creativity and complex communication.

questions.stem: The author suggests that tax policies be aimed at
options: increasing the return on capital investment.
easing the hostility between rich and poor.
preventing the income gap from widening.
questions.explain:
正确项：preventing the income gap from widening. 自动化可能扩大资本收入与劳动收入之间的差距，因此作者建议降低低工资劳动税负并扩大工资补贴，以提高收入并减少不平等。其目标正是防止收入差距继续扩大。
其他选项：A. encouraging the development of automation.：税收建议针对的是收入分配和就业激励，而非推动自动化发展，主体目的错位。；B. increasing the return on capital investment.：作者关注劳动收入受到挤压，政策要缩小资本与劳动收入差距；提高资本回报反而可能加剧问题。；C. easing the hostility between rich and poor.：原文说的是减少经济上的 inequality，没有提到富人和穷人之间的敌意，属于无中生有。
questions.evidence:
Finally, because automation threatens to widen the gap between capital income and labor income, taxes and the safety net will have to be rethought.
Taxes on low-wage labor need to be cut, and wage subsidies such as the earned income tax credit should be expanded: This would boost incomes, encourage work, reward companies for job creation, and reduce inequality.

questions.stem: In this text, the author presents a problem with
questions.explain:
正确项：possible solutions to it. 文章先提出自动化威胁中产就业的问题，随后以 The first step 等信号依次提出教育培训、创业环境、税收与社会保障方面的解决办法，因此采用的是“提出问题并给出可能对策”的结构。
其他选项：A. opposing views on it.：文中虽提到乐观者看法，但这只是对技术长期收益的让步，不是围绕两派对立观点展开全文。；C. its alarming impacts.：文章并未集中渲染各种骇人后果，而是把主要篇幅用于分析并提出政策建议，概括不全。；D. its major variations.：全文没有给自动化问题分类或讨论其主要变体，属于无中生有。
questions.evidence:
The first step, as Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee argue in The Second Machine Age, should be rethinking education and job training.
The challenge of coping with automation underlines the need for the U.S. to revive its fading business dynamism: Starting new companies must be made easier.
But policies to help workers adapt will be indispensable.

reading.title: Text 2
reading.en_title: A new survey by Harvard University finds more than two-thirds of young…
reading.cn_title: 年轻人对政治信息传播渠道的态度
reading.topic: 年轻人对政治信息传播渠道的态度
reading.intro: 本篇主题：年轻人对政治信息传播渠道的态度。先读题干，圈出关键词；回原文找证据句，再用主体、范围、方向排除。

paragraphs.en: A new survey by Harvard University finds more than two-thirds of young Americans disapprove of President Trump’s use of Twitter. The implication is that Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, not a president’s social media platform.
paragraphs.zh: 哈佛大学的一项新调查发现，超过三分之二的美国年轻人不赞成特朗普总统使用推特的方式。 这意味着，千禧一代更希望来自白宫的新闻经过其他信息来源的筛选，而不是直接出自总统的社交媒体平台。

paragraphs.en: Most Americans rely on social media to check daily headlines. Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills. Such a trend is badly needed. During the 2016 presidential campaign, nearly a quarter of web content shared by Twitter users in the politically critical state of Michigan was fake news, according to the University of Oxford. And a survey conducted for BuzzFeed News found 44 percent of Facebook users rarely or never trust news from the media giant.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数美国人依靠社交媒体浏览每日新闻标题。 然而，随着人们对各种媒体的不信任不断上升，他们或许正开始强化自己的媒介素养。 这种趋势正是当下迫切需要的。 牛津大学的研究显示，在 2016 年总统竞选期间，政治上至关重要的密歇根州内，推特用户所分享的网络内容有近四分之一是假新闻。 而为 BuzzFeed News 所做的一项调查发现，44% 的 Facebook 用户很少信任或从不信任这家媒体巨头提供的新闻。

paragraphs.en: Young people who are digital natives are indeed becoming more skillful at separating fact from fiction in cyberspace. A Knight Foundation focus-group survey of young people between ages 14 and 24 found they use “distributed trust” to verify stories. They cross-check sources and prefer news from different perspectives – especially those that are open about any bias. “Many young people assume a great deal of personal responsibility for educating themselves and actively seeking out opposing viewpoints,” the survey concluded.
paragraphs.zh: 作为数字原住民的年轻人确实越来越善于在网络空间中辨别事实与虚构。 奈特基金会对 14 至 24 岁年轻人开展的一项焦点小组调查发现，他们会利用“分布式信任”来核实新闻报道。 他们会交叉核对信息来源，并更愿意选择来自不同视角的新闻，尤其是那些会坦诚说明自身偏见的来源。 “许多年轻人主动承担起很大一部分责任，自我学习并积极寻找对立观点，”该调查总结道。

paragraphs.en: Such active research can have another effect. A 2014 survey conducted in Australia, Britain, and the United States by the University of Wisconsin-Madison found that young people’s reliance on social media led to greater political engagement.
paragraphs.zh: 这种主动查证还可能产生另一种影响。 威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校 2014 年在澳大利亚、英国和美国开展的一项调查发现，年轻人依赖社交媒体会使其政治参与度提高。

paragraphs.en: Social media allows users to experience news events more intimately and immediately while also permitting them to re-share news as a projection of their values and interests. This forces users to be more conscious of their role in passing along information. A survey by Barna research group found the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is “reader error,” more so than made-up stories or factual mistakes in reporting. About a third say the problem of fake news lies in “misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news” via social media. In other words, the choice to share news on social media may be at the heart of the issue. “This indicates there is a real personal responsibility in counteracting this problem,” says Roxanne Stone, editor in chief at Barna Group.
paragraphs.zh: 社交媒体让用户能够以更贴近、更即时的方式感受新闻事件，同时也允许他们把转发新闻当作自身价值观和兴趣的投射。 这就迫使用户更加清楚地意识到自己在传播信息时所扮演的角色。 巴纳研究集团的一项调查发现，美国人认为假新闻现象的首要原因是“读者错误”，其影响甚至超过了编造报道或新闻报道中的事实错误。 约三分之一的受访者认为，假新闻问题在于真实新闻在社交媒体上遭到“误读或夸大”。 换言之，是否选择在社交媒体上分享新闻，或许正是问题的核心所在。 “这表明，在抵制这一问题的过程中，个人确实负有责任，”巴纳集团主编罗克珊·斯通说道。

paragraphs.en: So when young people are critical of an over-tweeting president, they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills – and in their choices on when to share on social media.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，当年轻人批评一位发推过度的总统时，他们展现出一种思维上的自律——这种自律既体现在思考能力上，也体现在他们对何时在社交媒体上分享信息的选择上。

questions.stem: According to Paragraphs 1 and 2, many young Americans cast doubts on
options: the justification of the news-filtering practice.
people’s preference for social media platforms.
the administration’s ability to handle information.
social media as a reliable source of news.
questions.explain:
正确项：social media as a reliable source of news. 年轻人不愿把总统的社交媒体平台直接当作白宫新闻来源，而 44% 的 Facebook 用户很少或从不信任平台新闻。这些信息共同说明他们怀疑社交媒体能否成为可靠的新闻来源。
其他选项：A. the justification of the news-filtering practice.：年轻人恰恰希望新闻通过其他来源得到筛选，并未质疑这种筛选做法的正当性，与原文相反。；B. people’s preference for social media platforms.：原文说多数人依靠社交媒体查看标题，但题目问的是年轻人怀疑什么；其怀疑对象是新闻可靠性，而非人们的平台偏好。；C. the administration’s ability to handle information.：文章没有评价政府处理信息的能力，属于无中生有。
questions.evidence:
The implication is that Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, not a president’s social media platform.
And a survey conducted for BuzzFeed News found 44 percent of Facebook users rarely or never trust news from the media giant.

questions.stem: The phrase “beef up” (Line 2, Para. 2) is closest in meaning to
questions.explain:
正确项：sharpen. beef up 在此表示加强、提高媒介素养技能；sharpen skills 同样表示磨炼、提升技能，语义最接近。
其他选项：B. define.：意为“界定、定义”，不能表达使技能变强。；C. boast.：意为“自夸、吹嘘”，与提升媒介素养无关。；D. share.：意为“分享”，文中被加强的是技能，不是把技能分享给别人。
questions.evidence: Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills.

questions.stem: According to the Knight Foundation survey, young people
options: tend to voice their opinions in cyberspace.
verify news by referring to diverse sources.
have a strong sense of responsibility.
like to exchange views on “distributed trust”.
questions.explain:
正确项：verify news by referring to diverse sources. 调查发现，年轻人使用“分布式信任”核实报道：他们交叉核对信息来源，并偏好不同视角的新闻。选项中的 diverse sources 准确概括了这种多源验证行为。
其他选项：A. tend to voice their opinions in cyberspace.：原文说年轻人核实新闻、寻找相反观点，没有说他们倾向于在网上发表自己的意见。；C. have a strong sense of responsibility.：原文把责任具体限定为自我教育和主动寻找相反观点；该项把具体的信息核验行为泛化成笼统的责任感，不如 B 精确。；D. like to exchange views on “distributed trust”.：distributed trust 是他们用来验证新闻的方法，不是他们喜欢讨论或交换观点的话题，属于误解术语。
questions.evidence:
A Knight Foundation focus-group survey of young people between ages 14 and 24 found they use “distributed trust” to verify stories.
They cross-check sources and prefer news from different perspectives – especially those that are open about any bias.

questions.stem: The Barna survey found that a main cause for the fake news problem is
questions.explain:
正确项：readers’ misinterpretation. 巴纳调查把首要原因概括为 reader error，并进一步具体说明为读者在社交媒体上对真实新闻的 misinterpretation or exaggeration，因此答案是读者误读。
其他选项：A. readers’ outdated values.：原文谈的是读者误读、夸大和转发选择，没有说其价值观过时。；B. journalists’ biased reporting.：文中虽提到新闻来源可能存在偏见，但巴纳调查没有把记者的偏见报道列为假新闻的主要原因。；D. journalists’ made-up stories.：made-up stories 被用作对比项，调查认为 reader error 比编造报道更主要；该项颠倒了比较关系。
questions.evidence:
A survey by Barna research group found the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is “reader error,” more so than made-up stories or factual mistakes in reporting.
About a third say the problem of fake news lies in “misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news” via social media.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?
options: A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online.
A Counteraction Against the Over-tweeting Trend.
The Accumulation of Mutual Trust on SocialMedia.
The Platforms for Projection of Personal Interests.
questions.explain:
正确项：A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online. 全文围绕年轻人提升媒介素养展开：他们会辨别信息真伪、交叉核查来源，并对何时转发新闻作出更审慎的选择。该标题同时覆盖“批判性技能”和“网络新闻分享”两条主线。
其他选项：B. A Counteraction Against the Over-tweeting Trend.：总统过度发推只是文章的切入点和结尾回扣，全文并非介绍一场反对过度发推的行动，范围过窄。；C. The Accumulation of Mutual Trust on SocialMedia.：原文说对媒体的不信任正在上升；“分布式信任”指多源核验，不是社交媒体上的相互信任逐渐累积。；D. The Platforms for Projection of Personal Interests.：价值观和兴趣的投射只是解释转发行为的一处细节，不能涵盖全文关于辨识与分享责任的核心。
questions.evidence:
Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills.
Young people who are digital natives are indeed becoming more skillful at separating fact from fiction in cyberspace.
So when young people are critical of an over-tweeting president, they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills – and in their choices on when to share on social media.

reading.title: Text 3
reading.en_title: Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain’…
reading.cn_title: 医疗数据共享中的隐私与监管问题
reading.topic: 医疗数据共享中的隐私与监管问题
reading.intro: 本篇主题：医疗数据共享中的隐私与监管问题。先读题干，圈出关键词；回原文找证据句，再用主体、范围、方向排除。

paragraphs.en: Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain’s National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world. The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants. It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients’ rights and their expectations of privacy.
paragraphs.zh: 任何公允地评估英国国民医疗服务体系（NHS）与 DeepMind 之间这项协议所含风险的做法，都必须首先承认双方的本意是好的。 DeepMind 是全球领先的人工智能（AI）公司之一。 把这项工作应用于医疗保健的潜力十分巨大，但它也可能使权力进一步集中到科技巨头手中。 正是在这一背景下，信息专员伊丽莎白·德纳姆对 NHS 旗下的皇家自由医院信托作出了措辞严厉的裁定：该信托在 2015 年依据一份含糊的协议，将 160 万名患者的记录交给 DeepMind，而这份协议远远没有充分顾及患者的权利及其对隐私的合理期待。

paragraphs.en: DeepMind has almost apologized. The NHS trust has mended its ways. Further arrangements – and there may be many – between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn. But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it “controlled” the data and DeepMind merely “processed” it. But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value.
paragraphs.zh: DeepMind 几乎已经道了歉，但还算不上正式道歉。 NHS 医疗信托已经改正了原先的做法。 NHS 与 DeepMind 之间后续的合作安排——而且可能会有很多——都将受到仔细审查，以确保已经向患者征得所有必要许可，并且已经清除全部非必要数据。 在患者知情同意方面，仍有需要吸取的教训。 但是，隐私并不是看待本案的唯一角度，甚至不是最重要的角度。 德纳姆女士选择把责任集中归于 NHS 医疗信托，因为按照现行法律，是该信托“控制”数据，而 DeepMind 只是“处理”数据。 但这种区分没有抓住关键：真正赋予数据价值的是对数据的处理与汇总，而不是仅仅占有一个个数据片段。

paragraphs.en: The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate. Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them. That misses the way the surveillance economy works. The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more.
paragraphs.zh: 真正重大的问题是：谁应当从对我们如今生活所产生的全部数据的分析中获益。 隐私法建立在这样一种损害概念之上：可识别个人身份的信息会对该个人造成伤害。 这种思路没有把握监控经济的运行方式。 在监控经济中，一个人的数据只有与另外数以千万计的人的数据进行比较时，才会获得价值。

paragraphs.en: The use of privacy law to curb the tech giants in this instance feels slightly maladapted. This practice does not address the real worry. It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives. What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources. If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as a big pharma has done. We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism. Ms Denham’s report is a welcome start.
paragraphs.zh: 在本案中，借助隐私法约束科技巨头，似乎有些不得要领。 这种做法没有回应真正令人担忧的问题。 仅仅声称 DeepMind 开发的算法将使患者受益并挽救生命，是不够的。 真正要紧的是，这些算法将归一个私人垄断者所有，而该垄断者是利用公共资源开发出它们的。 如果软件有望像如今的药物那样大规模挽救生命，那么人们也可以预料，大数据企业会像大型制药公司过去那样行事。 我们仍处在这场革命的开端，而今天看似微小的选择，日后可能会产生极其重大的后果。 要避免一个数字封建主义的未来，还需要进行长期斗争。 德纳姆女士的报告是一个令人欣慰的开端。

questions.stem: What is true of the agreement between the NHS and DeepMind?
options: It caused conflicts among tech giants.
It failed to pay due attention to patients’ rights.
It fell short of the latter’s expectations.
It put both sides into a dangerous situation.
questions.explain:
正确项：It failed to pay due attention to patients’ rights. 原文说这份含糊的协议 took far too little account of the patients’ rights，即远未充分顾及患者权利和隐私期待。failed to pay due attention to 是这一表述的同义改写。
其他选项：A. It caused conflicts among tech giants.：文章担忧权力集中于科技巨头，但没有说该协议造成科技巨头之间的冲突，属于无中生有。；C. It fell short of the latter’s expectations.：原文说协议没有满足患者对隐私的期待；the latter 指双方中后者 DeepMind，主体被偷换。；D. It put both sides into a dangerous situation.：作者评估的是协议带来的制度风险，没有说 NHS 和 DeepMind 双方都陷入危险处境，属于过度推断。
questions.evidence: It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients’ rights and their expectations of privacy.

questions.stem: The NHS trust responded to Denham’s verdict with
questions.explain:
正确项：necessary adjustments. mended its ways 表明 NHS 信托已经改正做法；后续协议将接受审查、征得患者许可并清除不必要数据，这些都是必要调整的具体内容。
其他选项：A. empty promises.：原文列出了审查、许可和清除数据等实质性措施，并非空洞承诺。；B. tough resistance.：NHS 信托选择整改而非强硬抵抗，与原文相反。；D. sincere apologies.：almost apologized 的主体是 DeepMind，而且“几乎道歉”也不等于真诚道歉；该项同时混淆主体和程度。
questions.evidence:
The NHS trust has mended its ways.
Further arrangements – and there may be many – between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned.

questions.stem: The author argues in Paragraph 2 that
options: privacy protection must be secured at all costs.
leaking patients’ data is worse than selling it.
making profits from patients’ data is illegal.
the value of data comes from the processing of it.
questions.explain:
正确项：the value of data comes from the processing of it. 作者用强调句指出，赋予数据价值的是 processing and aggregation，而不是仅仅占有数据片段。选项准确保留了“数据处理创造价值”这一核心关系。
其他选项：A. privacy protection must be secured at all costs.：作者认为隐私重要，但明确说隐私并非本案唯一甚至最重要的角度；at all costs 绝对化且与原文不符。；B. leaking patients’ data is worse than selling it.：文章没有比较泄露数据与出售数据的严重程度，属于无中生有。；C. making profits from patients’ data is illegal.：作者讨论利益归属和垄断风险，没有作出“利用患者数据获利违法”的法律判断。
questions.evidence: But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value.

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, the real worry arising from this deal is
options: the vicious rivalry among big pharmas.
the ineffective enforcement of privacy law.
the uncontrolled use of new software.
the monopoly of big data by tech giants.
questions.explain:
正确项：the monopoly of big data by tech giants. 作者说真正要紧的是，利用公共资源和患者数据开发出的算法会归私人垄断者所有；结合全文对权力向科技巨头集中的担忧，可知核心风险是科技巨头垄断大数据及其价值。
其他选项：A. the vicious rivalry among big pharmas.：制药巨头只是类比对象，文章没有讨论它们之间的恶性竞争。；B. the ineffective enforcement of privacy law.：作者认为隐私法本身不完全适配真正问题，而不是抱怨该法律执行不力，偷换了批评对象。；C. the uncontrolled use of new software.：原文承认算法能造福患者，担忧的是算法和数据价值的私人所有与垄断，不是软件使用完全失控。
questions.evidence: What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources.

questions.stem: The author’s attitude toward the application of AI to healthcare is
questions.explain:
正确项：cautious. 作者承认医疗 AI 潜力巨大，却反复警示权力集中、私人垄断和早期选择的长期后果，并主张持续监管。这是一种认可价值但警惕风险的谨慎态度。
其他选项：A. ambiguous.：作者态度并不含糊；他明确肯定医疗潜力，同时明确要求防范垄断风险，属于有依据的审慎而非模棱两可。；C. appreciative.：作者只肯定其潜力和善意，大量篇幅用于分析风险；单纯“赞赏”忽略了文章的警示重心。；D. contemptuous.：文中没有鄙视或轻蔑 AI，反而承认它能造福患者、挽救生命，感情色彩错误。
questions.evidence:
The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants.
We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later.
A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism.

reading.title: Text 4
reading.en_title: The U.S. Postal Service (USPS) continues to bleed red ink. It reported…
reading.cn_title: 美国邮政系统的财务困境与改革方向
reading.topic: 美国邮政系统的财务困境与改革方向
reading.intro: 本篇主题：美国邮政系统的财务困境与改革方向。先读题干，圈出关键词；回原文找证据句，再用主体、范围、方向排除。

paragraphs.en: The U.S. Postal Service (USPS) continues to bleed red ink. It reported a net loss of $5.6 billion for fiscal 2016, the 10th straight year its expenses have exceeded revenue. Meanwhile, it has more than $120 billion in unfunded liabilities, mostly for employee health and retirement costs. There are many reasons this formerly stable federal institution finds itself at the brink of bankruptcy. Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its bread-and-butter product, first-class mail, and a regulatory structure that denies management the flexibility to adjust its operations to the new reality.
paragraphs.zh: 美国邮政署（USPS）仍在持续亏损。 美国邮政署报告称，2016 财年的净亏损为 56 亿美元；这已是其支出连续第十年超过收入。 与此同时，它还有超过 1,200 亿美元的无资金保障负债，主要来自员工医疗和退休成本。 这个曾经稳定的联邦机构如今发现自己濒临破产，背后存在许多原因。 从根本上说，美国邮政署陷入了前所未有的两面夹击：一边是技术变革永久性地削弱了对其支柱产品——一类邮件——的需求；另一边是监管结构不允许管理层灵活调整运营以适应新的现实。

paragraphs.en: And interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers exert self-interested pressure on the USPS’s ultimate overseer – Congress – insisting that whatever else happens to the Postal Service, aspects of the status quo they depend on get protected. This is why repeated attempts at reform legislation have failed in recent years, leaving the Postal Service unable to pay its bills except by deferring vital modernization.
paragraphs.zh: 而从邮政工会到贺卡制造商，各类利益集团都出于自身利益向美国邮政署的最高监督者——国会——施压，坚持认为无论邮政系统还会发生什么变化，它们所依赖的那些现状都必须受到保护。 这正是近年来一次次邮政改革立法尝试均告失败的原因，结果美国邮政署除了推迟至关重要的现代化改造之外，已无力支付各项账单。

paragraphs.en: Now comes word that everyone involved – Democrats, Republicans, the Postal Service, the unions and the system’s heaviest users – has finally agreed on a plan to fix the system. Legislation is moving through the House that would save USPS an estimated $28.6 billion over five years, which could help pay for new vehicles, among other survival measures. Most of the money would come from a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase and from shifting postal retirees into Medicare. The latter step would largely offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care, thus addressing a long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions.
paragraphs.zh: 如今传来消息：所有相关方——民主党人、共和党人、美国邮政署、工会以及邮政系统的最大用户——终于就一项修复该系统的方案达成了一致。 一项法案正在众议院推进，预计可在五年内为美国邮政署节省 286 亿美元；除其他维持生存的措施外，这笔钱还可以帮助购买新车辆。 大部分资金将来自两项措施：永久性地将每封信的邮资提高一美分，以及把邮政退休人员纳入联邦医疗保险计划。 后一项措施将大幅抵消每年预先为退休人员医疗保障筹资所造成的财务负担，从而回应美国邮政署及其工会长期以来的一项不满。

paragraphs.en: If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate – where someone is bound to point out that it amounts to the bare, bare minimum necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, not comprehensive reform. There’s no change to collective bargaining at the USPS, a major omission considering that personnel accounts for 80 percent of the agency’s costs. Also missing is any discussion of eliminating Saturday letter delivery. That common-sense change enjoys wide public support and would save the USPS $2 billion per year. But postal special-interest groups seem to have killed it, at least in the House. The emerging consensus around the bill is a sign that legislators are getting frightened about a politically embarrassing short-term collapse at the USPS. It is not, however, a sign that they’re getting serious about transforming the postal system for the 21stcentury.
paragraphs.zh: 即便该措施在众议院获得通过，它仍须过参议院这一关——在那里必定会有人指出，它不过是维持美国邮政署生存所必需的最低限度措施，远非全面改革。 该方案没有改变美国邮政署的集体谈判制度；考虑到人员成本占该机构总成本的 80%，这是一个重大遗漏。 同样缺失的，还有关于取消周六信件投递的任何讨论。 这一符合常理的改革得到公众广泛支持，而且每年可为美国邮政署节省 20 亿美元。 但是，邮政特殊利益集团似乎已经扼杀了这项改革，至少在众议院是如此。 围绕这项法案逐渐形成的共识表明，立法者开始害怕美国邮政署在短期内崩溃，因为那会令他们在政治上难堪。 然而，这并不表明他们开始认真推动邮政系统转型，以适应 21 世纪。

questions.stem: The financial problem with the USPS is caused partly by
questions.explain:
正确项：its rigid management. 原文指出，监管结构使管理层失去根据新现实调整运营的灵活性。选项用 rigid management 概括这种受到制度约束、无法灵活调整的管理状态，因此它是财务困境的部分成因。
其他选项：A. its unbalanced budget.：支出超过收入和巨额亏损是财务问题的表现或结果，并非本句分析的根本成因，属于因果层级错位。；C. the cost for technical upgrading.：原文说 USPS 因缺钱而推迟现代化，并未说技术升级成本导致财务困境，因果倒置。；D. the withdrawal of bank support.：全文没有提及银行撤回支持，属于无中生有。
questions.evidence: Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its bread-and-butter product, first-class mail, and a regulatory structure that denies management the flexibility to adjust its operations to the new reality.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, the USPS fails to modernize itself due to
options: the shrinking demand for postal service.
questions.explain:
正确项：the interference from interest groups. 邮政工会、贺卡制造商等利益集团向国会施压，要求保护各自依赖的现状，由此导致改革立法失败，USPS 只能推迟关键的现代化改造。因果链直接指向利益集团干预。
其他选项：B. the inadequate funding from Congress.：第二段批评国会受到利益集团影响，没有说国会拨款不足导致现代化失败。；C. the shrinking demand for postal service.：需求下降出现在第一段，是整体财务压力的一端；第二段明确说明改革和现代化受阻的原因是利益集团干预。；D. the incompetence of postal unions.：工会只是多个利益集团之一，原文批评其自利施压，并未说工会能力不足；同时该项错误缩小主体范围。
questions.evidence:
And interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers exert self-interested pressure on the USPS’s ultimate overseer – Congress – insisting that whatever else happens to the Postal Service, aspects of the status quo they depend on get protected.
This is why repeated attempts at reform legislation have failed in recent years, leaving the Postal Service unable to pay its bills except by deferring vital modernization.

questions.stem: The long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions can be addressed by
options: removing its burden of retiree health care.
making more investment in new vehicles.
questions.explain:
正确项：removing its burden of retiree health care. the latter step 指把邮政退休人员纳入 Medicare；这会大幅抵消 USPS 每年预先筹措退休人员医疗资金的负担，从而回应长期不满。选项用 removing its burden 概括减轻这一负担。
其他选项：B. making more investment in new vehicles.：购置新车只是节省资金后可采取的求生措施之一，不是长期不满所针对的问题。；C. adopting a new rate-increase mechanism.：每封信永久加价一美分是另一项资金来源；the latter step 明确排除它。；D. attracting more first-class mail users.：原文说一类邮件需求已永久下降，没有提出吸引更多用户来解决退休医疗负担。
questions.evidence:
Most of the money would come from a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase and from shifting postal retirees into Medicare.
The latter step would largely offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care, thus addressing a long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions.

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, the author seems to view legislators with
questions.explain:
正确项：discontent. 作者把法案称为“最低限度”而非全面改革，批评重大遗漏和利益集团阻挠，并断言立法者没有认真推动转型。这些明显的负面评价体现的是不满。
其他选项：A. respect.：文中没有赞扬立法者的能力或担当，反而批评他们只担心短期政治难堪。；B. tolerance.：作者不是宽容地接受不完善方案，而是连续指出其不足，语气明显带有批评。；D. gratitude.：虽有跨党派共识，但作者认为这并非认真改革的迹象，没有表达感激。
questions.evidence:
If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate – where someone is bound to point out that it amounts to the bare, bare minimum necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, not comprehensive reform.
That common-sense change enjoys wide public support and would save the USPS $2 billion per year.
But postal special-interest groups seem to have killed it, at least in the House.
It is not, however, a sign that they’re getting serious about transforming the postal system for the 21stcentury.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?
options: The USPS Starts to Miss Its Good Old Days.
The Postal Service: Keep Away from My Cheese.
The USPS: Chronic Illness Requires a Quick Cure.
The Postal Service Needs More Than a Band-Aid.
questions.explain:
正确项：The Postal Service Needs More Than a Band-Aid. USPS 的困境源于需求下降、监管僵化和利益集团阻挠等长期结构性问题；现有法案只提供维持生存的最低限度救助，并非全面改革。Band-Aid 比喻临时、表面的补救，标题准确表达“需要更深层改革”的主旨。
其他选项：A. The USPS Starts to Miss Its Good Old Days.：文章提到 USPS 曾经稳定，但没有描写其怀念过去；该项把制度改革议题改写成情绪问题。；B. The Postal Service: Keep Away from My Cheese.：该标题可联想到利益集团保护既得利益，却无法涵盖财务危机、救助方案及全面改革不足，重心过窄。；C. The USPS: Chronic Illness Requires a Quick Cure.：USPS 的问题确属长期积累，但作者要求的是全面、结构性的改革，而不是强调“快速治疗”；Quick Cure 与论旨不符。
questions.evidence:
If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate – where someone is bound to point out that it amounts to the bare, bare minimum necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, not comprehensive reform.
It is not, however, a sign that they’re getting serious about transforming the postal system for the 21stcentury.

sentences.en: Among the annoying challenges facing the middle class is one that will probably go unmentioned in the next presidential campaign: What happens when the robots come for their jobs?
sentences.core: Among the annoying challenges ... is one ...，即“诸多挑战中有一个挑战”，是地点状语前置引起的完全倒装。
sentences.structure: facing the middle class 是现在分词短语，修饰 challenges；that will probably go unmentioned ... 是定语从句，修饰 one；冒号后的疑问句具体说明这个挑战是什么。
sentences.key: come for：常见义为“来取、来找”；此处带有威胁意味，指机器人“冲着中产阶层的工作而来、要取代这些岗位”。
sentences.zh: 中产阶层面临着种种恼人的挑战，其中有一个很可能不会在下一届总统竞选中被提及：当机器人来抢他们的工作时，会发生什么？
sentences.tip: their 指 the middle class（中产阶层群体），不是 robots。

sentences.en: About half of U.S. jobs are at high risk of being automated, according to a University of Oxford study, with the middle class disproportionately squeezed.
sentences.core: About half of U.S. jobs are at high risk of being automated.
sentences.structure: according to ... 交代信息来源；with the middle class disproportionately squeezed 是 with + 宾语 + 过去分词 的独立结构，补充说明中产阶层承受的影响并不成比例地更大。
sentences.key: squeeze：常见义为“挤压”；此处作比喻，表示中产阶层的就业空间和收入机会遭到压缩。
sentences.zh: 牛津大学的一项研究显示，美国约有一半的工作面临被自动化取代的高风险，而中产阶层受到的挤压尤其严重。
sentences.tip: disproportionately 不是说中产阶层人数多，而是说其所受冲击相对于其他群体格外严重。

sentences.en: But many middle-class occupations – trucking, financial advice, software engineering – have aroused their interest, or soon will.
sentences.core: Many middle-class occupations have aroused their interest, or soon will.
sentences.structure: 两个破折号之间列举中产职业；or soon will 是省略结构，完整形式为 or soon will arouse their interest。
sentences.key: arouse one’s interest：引起某人的兴趣；此处继续使用拟人，意为这些职业已经或即将成为自动化取代的对象。
sentences.zh: 但许多中产阶层从事的职业——货运、财务咨询、软件工程——已经引起了机器人的“兴趣”，即使现在还没有，也很快会如此。
sentences.tip: their 指上一句中的 robots；不是这些职业引起了中产阶层的兴趣。

sentences.en: The Industrial Revolution didn’t go so well for Luddites whose jobs were displaced by mechanized looms, but it eventually raised living standards and created more jobs than it destroyed.
sentences.core: The Industrial Revolution didn’t go so well for Luddites, but it raised living standards and created more jobs.
sentences.structure: whose jobs were displaced ... 是定语从句，修饰 Luddites；than it destroyed 是比较从句，与 more jobs 呼应，destroyed 后省略 jobs。
sentences.key: Luddite：卢德派成员；历史上指反对机器取代手工业劳动的工人，此处也带有“抵制技术变革者”的含义。；displace jobs：取代、消灭工作岗位。
sentences.zh: 工业革命对卢德派工人而言并不顺利，他们的工作被机械织布机取代；但工业革命最终提高了生活水平，而且创造的工作岗位比摧毁的更多。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Likewise, automation should eventually boost productivity, stimulate demand by driving down prices, and free workers from hard, boring work.
sentences.core: Automation should boost ..., stimulate ..., and free ...，三个动词短语并列作谓语。
sentences.structure: by driving down prices 作方式状语，直接说明如何 stimulate demand，不修饰另外两个并列谓语。
sentences.key: boost productivity：提高生产率。；drive down prices：压低价格。；free sb. from ...：使某人摆脱……。
sentences.zh: 同样，自动化最终应当能够提高生产率、通过压低价格来刺激需求，并把劳动者从艰苦乏味的工作中解放出来。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: The first step, as Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee argue in The Second Machine Age, should be rethinking education and job training.
sentences.core: The first step should be rethinking education and job training.
sentences.structure: as ... argue in ... 是插入的方式状语从句，意为“正如……所主张的”；rethinking ... 是动名词短语作表语，说明第一步的具体内容。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 正如埃里克·布莱恩约尔松和安德鲁·麦卡菲在《第二次机器革命》中所主张的，第一步应当是重新思考教育与职业培训。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Curriculums – from grammar school to college – should evolve to focus less on memorizing facts and more on creativity and complex communication.
sentences.core: Curriculums should evolve.
sentences.structure: 破折号之间的 from grammar school to college 说明课程改革覆盖的教育阶段；to focus ... 表示课程调整的方向；less on ... and more on ... 构成对比。
sentences.key: grammar school：此处按美国教育语境指“小学”，不是“语法学校”。；evolve：常见义为“进化”；此处指课程体系“逐步发展、调整”。；focus less on A and more on B：减少对 A 的关注，更多关注 B。；memorize facts：记忆事实性知识。
sentences.zh: 从小学到大学，课程都应当逐步调整，减少对事实记忆的关注，更多培养创造力和复杂沟通能力。
sentences.tip: 答案对应的是 creativity（创造潜能），而不是泛泛的个人需求或求职技巧。

sentences.en: Professionals trying to acquire new skills will be able to do so without going into debt.
sentences.core: Professionals will be able to do so.
sentences.structure: trying to acquire new skills 是现在分词短语，修饰 Professionals；do so 代替上文所说的接受额外培训、掌握新技能；without going into debt 作方式状语。
sentences.key: acquire new skills：掌握新技能。；go into debt：陷入债务、负债。
sentences.zh: 希望掌握新技能的专业人士将能够在不负债的情况下接受这类培训。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: The challenge of coping with automation underlines the need for the U.S. to revive its fading business dynamism: Starting new companies must be made easier.
sentences.core: The challenge underlines the need: Starting new companies must be made easier.
sentences.structure: of coping with automation 修饰 challenge；for the U.S. to revive ... 说明 need 的具体内容；冒号后的被动句进一步给出重振商业活力的办法。
sentences.key: underline：常见义为“在……下画线”；此处作动词，意为“突出、强调”。；business dynamism：指企业不断创立、扩张、退出所体现的经济活力，不只是“商业动力”。
sentences.zh: 应对自动化的挑战凸显出美国重振其日渐衰退的商业活力的必要性：必须降低创办新公司的难度。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: The U.S. needs the new companies that will invent them.
sentences.core: The U.S. needs the new companies.
sentences.structure: that will invent them 是定语从句，修饰 the new companies；them 指上一句的 the best uses，不是 3D 打印机和虚拟现实本身。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 美国需要由新公司来开发这些最佳用途。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Finally, because automation threatens to widen the gap between capital income and labor income, taxes and the safety net will have to be rethought.
sentences.core: Taxes and the safety net will have to be rethought.
sentences.structure: because ... 是原因状语从句；threatens to widen ... 表示自动化有造成收入差距扩大的风险；between A and B 界定差距的两端。
sentences.key: safety net：字面义为“安全网”；此处指为失业者和低收入者提供保障的社会福利制度。；rethink：不是简单地“再想一遍”，而是“重新审视并调整”。
sentences.zh: 最后，由于自动化可能扩大资本收入与劳动收入之间的差距，税收制度和社会保障体系都必须重新设计。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Taxes on low-wage labor need to be cut, and wage subsidies such as the earned income tax credit should be expanded: This would boost incomes, encourage work, reward companies for job creation, and reduce inequality.
sentences.core: Taxes ... need to be cut, and wage subsidies ... should be expanded: This would boost ..., encourage ..., reward ..., and reduce ... .
sentences.structure: 冒号前提出两项并列政策；such as ... 举例说明工资补贴；冒号后的 This 指代前述减税与扩大补贴这一整套做法；四个并列动词说明政策效果。
sentences.key: wage subsidy：工资补贴；通过公共政策提高劳动者的实际所得。；earned income tax credit：劳动所得税抵免，美国面向中低收入劳动者的税收补助政策。；reward companies for job creation：因企业创造就业岗位而给予激励。
sentences.zh: 应当降低针对低工资劳动的税负，并扩大劳动所得税抵免等工资补贴：这样做既能提高收入、鼓励就业，也能奖励创造岗位的企业并缩小不平等。
sentences.tip: 这些税收政策的最终指向是阻止收入差距继续扩大，而不是鼓励自动化本身或提高资本回报。

sentences.en: Technology will improve society in ways big and small over the next few years, yet this will be little comfort to those who find their lives and careers upended by automation.
sentences.core: Technology will improve society, yet this will be little comfort to those.
sentences.structure: in ways big and small 表示影响方式不论大小；who find ... 是定语从句，修饰 those；their lives and careers upended 是 find + 宾语 + 过去分词作宾补 结构。
sentences.key: upend：本义为“使倒立”；此处意为“彻底打乱、颠覆”。；little comfort：几乎算不上安慰；little 表否定含义。
sentences.zh: 未来几年，技术会从大大小小的方面改善社会；然而，对那些发现自己的生活和职业被自动化彻底打乱的人来说，这并不能带来多少安慰。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Destroying the machines that are coming for our jobs would be nuts.
sentences.core: Destroying the machines would be nuts.
sentences.structure: 动名词短语作主语；that are coming for our jobs 是定语从句，修饰 machines，并回扣首段的 robots come for their jobs。
sentences.key: nuts：口语形容词，意为“疯狂的、荒唐的”，不是“坚果”。
sentences.zh: 摧毁那些正要抢走我们工作的机器，无疑是疯狂之举。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: But policies to help workers adapt will be indispensable.
sentences.core: Policies will be indispensable.
sentences.structure: to help workers adapt 是不定式短语，后置修饰 policies，说明政策的目的和内容。
sentences.key: indispensable：不可或缺的、必不可少的。；be at high risk of being automated：面临被自动化取代的高风险。；be disproportionately squeezed：受到格外严重、不成比例的挤压。；drive down prices：压低价格。
sentences.zh: 但是，帮助劳动者适应这种变化的政策将不可或缺。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: The implication is that Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, not a president’s social media platform.
sentences.core: The implication is that Millennials prefer news ... to be filtered ... .
sentences.structure: that ... 引导表语从句；prefer + 宾语 + to be done 表示“更希望某事物被怎样处理”；not ... 排除总统的社交媒体平台这一直接来源。
sentences.key: filter：常见义为“过滤杂质”；此处指新闻经过其他媒体来源的核查、筛选和编辑。；Millennials：千禧一代，通常指出生并成长于数字化时代的一代人。
sentences.zh: 这意味着，千禧一代更希望来自白宫的新闻经过其他信息来源的筛选，而不是直接出自总统的社交媒体平台。
sentences.tip: 年轻人质疑的不是新闻筛选本身，恰恰是未经其他来源筛选、直接由总统社交账号发布信息的做法。

sentences.en: Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills.
sentences.core: People may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills.
sentences.structure: as distrust has risen toward all media 是伴随变化的状语从句，说明媒介素养提升的背景；may be starting to 表示谨慎推测，而非已经确定完成。
sentences.key: beef up：口语短语，意为“加强、充实、提高”，此处近义于选项中的 sharpen，与“牛肉”无关。；literacy：常见义为“读写能力”；media literacy 指辨识、理解和评估媒体信息的能力。
sentences.zh: 然而，随着人们对各种媒体的不信任不断上升，他们或许正开始强化自己的媒介素养。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: During the 2016 presidential campaign, nearly a quarter of web content shared by Twitter users in the politically critical state of Michigan was fake news, according to the University of Oxford.
sentences.core: Nearly a quarter of web content was fake news.
sentences.structure: shared by Twitter users 是过去分词短语，修饰 web content；in the politically critical state of Michigan 限定用户所在地区；according to ... 交代研究来源。
sentences.key: critical：常见义为“批判的”；此处意为“关键的、至关重要的”，强调密歇根州在选举政治中的重要性。
sentences.zh: 牛津大学的研究显示，在 2016 年总统竞选期间，政治上至关重要的密歇根州内，推特用户所分享的网络内容有近四分之一是假新闻。
sentences.tip: a quarter 指被分享的网络内容中约四分之一是假新闻，不是说四分之一的推特用户制造了假新闻。

sentences.en: And a survey conducted for BuzzFeed News found 44 percent of Facebook users rarely or never trust news from the media giant.
sentences.core: A survey found (that) 44 percent of Facebook users rarely or never trust news.
sentences.structure: conducted for BuzzFeed News 是过去分词短语，修饰 survey；found 后省略宾语从句连接词 that；from the media giant 修饰 news。
sentences.key: rarely or never trust：很少信任或从不信任。；the media giant：这家媒体巨头，回指 Facebook。
sentences.zh: 而为 BuzzFeed News 所做的一项调查发现，44% 的 Facebook 用户很少信任或从不信任这家媒体巨头提供的新闻。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Young people who are digital natives are indeed becoming more skillful at separating fact from fiction in cyberspace.
sentences.core: Young people are becoming more skillful.
sentences.structure: who are digital natives 是定语从句，修饰 Young people；at separating ... 说明他们越来越熟练的具体事项。
sentences.key: digital native：数字原住民，指从小接触数字技术并在数字环境中成长的人。；separate fact from fiction：辨别事实与虚构；识别信息真伪。；cyberspace：网络空间。
sentences.zh: 作为数字原住民的年轻人确实越来越善于在网络空间中辨别事实与虚构。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: A Knight Foundation focus-group survey of young people between ages 14 and 24 found they use “distributed trust” to verify stories.
sentences.core: A survey found (that) they use “distributed trust”.
sentences.structure: of young people between ages 14 and 24 说明调查对象；found 后省略 that；to verify stories 是目的状语。
sentences.key: focus-group survey：焦点小组调查，通过小组访谈了解受访者的看法与行为。；distributed trust：分布式信任，即不依赖单一权威来源，而是通过多个来源交叉验证信息。；verify stories：核实新闻报道。
sentences.zh: 奈特基金会对 14 至 24 岁年轻人开展的一项焦点小组调查发现，他们会利用“分布式信任”来核实新闻报道。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: They cross-check sources and prefer news from different perspectives – especially those that are open about any bias.
sentences.core: They cross-check sources and prefer news.
sentences.structure: 两个动词短语并列；from different perspectives 修饰 news；those that are open about any bias 中，those 代指不同的新闻来源，that ... 是定语从句。
sentences.key: be open about：坦诚说明、不隐瞒；此处不是“对……持开放态度”。；bias：偏见、倾向性；在新闻语境中指报道立场可能造成的偏向。；cross-check sources：交叉核对信息来源。；from different perspectives：来自不同视角。
sentences.zh: 他们会交叉核对信息来源，并更愿意选择来自不同视角的新闻，尤其是那些会坦诚说明自身偏见的来源。
sentences.tip: distributed trust 不是交流关于“分布式信任”的观点，而是参考多样来源并进行交叉核验的方法。

sentences.en: “Many young people assume a great deal of personal responsibility for educating themselves and actively seeking out opposing viewpoints,” the survey concluded.
sentences.core: The survey concluded, “Many young people assume ... responsibility.”
sentences.structure: 直接引语置于引述语之前；for educating themselves and actively seeking out ... 说明所承担责任的具体内容，两个动名词短语并列。
sentences.key: assume responsibility for：承担……的责任。；seek out opposing viewpoints：主动寻找相反的观点。
sentences.zh: “许多年轻人主动承担起很大一部分责任，自我学习并积极寻找对立观点，”该调查总结道。
sentences.tip: 这里的责任范围很具体，即自我教育并主动接触相反观点，不能扩大成笼统意义上的“责任感很强”。

sentences.en: A 2014 survey conducted in Australia, Britain, and the United States by the University of Wisconsin-Madison found that young people’s reliance on social media led to greater political engagement.
sentences.core: A survey found that young people’s reliance ... led to greater political engagement.
sentences.structure: conducted ... by ... 是过去分词短语，修饰 survey；其中地点状语在前、实施者由 by 引出；that ... 是 found 的宾语从句。
sentences.key: engagement：常见义为“订婚”或“约定”；此处意为“参与、投入”，political engagement 即政治参与。
sentences.zh: 威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校 2014 年在澳大利亚、英国和美国开展的一项调查发现，年轻人依赖社交媒体会使其政治参与度提高。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Social media allows users to experience news events more intimately and immediately while also permitting them to re-share news as a projection of their values and interests.
sentences.core: Social media allows users to experience ... while also permitting them to re-share ... .
sentences.structure: allow sb. to do 与 permit sb. to do 表达两个同时存在的作用；more intimately and immediately 修饰 experience；as a projection ... 说明转发行为所承担的功能。
sentences.key: intimately：常见义与“亲密”有关；此处指用户能够更贴近新闻事件、更有切身感。；projection：常见义为“预测、投影”；此处意为个人价值观和兴趣的“外在表达、投射”。；permit sb. to do sth.：允许某人做某事。；re-share news：再次分享、转发新闻。
sentences.zh: 社交媒体让用户能够以更贴近、更即时的方式感受新闻事件，同时也允许他们把转发新闻当作自身价值观和兴趣的投射。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: A survey by Barna research group found the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is “reader error,” more so than made-up stories or factual mistakes in reporting.
sentences.core: A survey found (that) the top reason ... is “reader error”.
sentences.structure: by Barna research group 修饰 survey；given by Americans 是过去分词短语，修饰 the top reason；for the fake news phenomenon 说明原因所针对的现象；more so than ... 把读者错误与编造报道、事实错误作比较。
sentences.key: top reason：首要原因、最主要的原因。；reader error：读者在理解、判断或转发信息时产生的错误。；more so than：比……更是如此；这里表示“读者错误”比后两类新闻生产端错误更被视为主要原因。
sentences.zh: 巴纳研究集团的一项调查发现，美国人认为假新闻现象的首要原因是“读者错误”，其影响甚至超过了编造报道或新闻报道中的事实错误。
sentences.tip: 调查强调的是读者端的错误，而不是把首要责任归给记者的偏见、编造或事实失误。

sentences.en: About a third say the problem of fake news lies in “misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news” via social media.
sentences.core: About a third say (that) the problem ... lies in “misinterpretation or exaggeration ...”.
sentences.structure: About a third 指约三分之一的受访者；say 后省略 that；of actual news 说明被误读或夸大的对象；via social media 说明这种信息变形发生和传播的渠道。
sentences.key: lie in：在于；问题或原因存在于某处。；misinterpretation or exaggeration：误读或夸大。；actual news：真实发生、确有事实依据的新闻。
sentences.zh: 约三分之一的受访者认为，假新闻问题在于真实新闻在社交媒体上遭到“误读或夸大”。
sentences.tip: 原文不是说读者持有“过时价值观”，而是说他们可能错误理解或夸大真实新闻。

sentences.en: “This indicates there is a real personal responsibility in counteracting this problem,” says Roxanne Stone, editor in chief at Barna Group.
sentences.core: Roxanne Stone says, “This indicates ... .”
sentences.structure: 直接引语前置；there is ... 是省略了连接词 that 的宾语从句；editor in chief at Barna Group 是 Roxanne Stone 的同位语。
sentences.key: counteract a problem：抵消、遏制某个问题造成的影响。；editor in chief：主编。
sentences.zh: “这表明，在抵制这一问题的过程中，个人确实负有责任，”巴纳集团主编罗克珊·斯通说道。
sentences.tip: This 指前文关于读者误读、夸大和选择性转发会助长假新闻的调查结论。

sentences.en: So when young people are critical of an over-tweeting president, they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills – and in their choices on when to share on social media.
sentences.core: When young people are critical ..., they reveal a mental discipline.
sentences.structure: when ... 是时间兼条件背景的状语从句；in thinking skills 与 in their choices ... 并列，具体说明这种自律表现在哪些方面；on when to share 中“疑问词 + 不定式”说明选择的内容。
sentences.key: be critical of：批评、不赞成；不是单纯“对……至关重要”。；discipline：常见义为“学科、纪律、惩罚”；此处指克制而审慎的“自律”。；over-tweeting：发推过多、过度使用推特发声。；filter news through other sources：通过其他来源筛选、核查新闻。
sentences.zh: 因此，当年轻人批评一位发推过度的总统时，他们展现出一种思维上的自律——这种自律既体现在思考能力上，也体现在他们对何时在社交媒体上分享信息的选择上。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain’s National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well.
sentences.core: Any fair-minded assessment must start by acknowledging ... .
sentences.structure: of the dangers 修饰 assessment；of the deal between ... and ... 继续限定风险来自哪项协议；by acknowledging that ... 说明评估的起点，其中 that ... 作 acknowledging 的宾语。
sentences.key: fair-minded：公正的、不偏不倚的。；assessment of the dangers：对风险的评估。；mean well：出于好意、本意良善。
sentences.zh: 任何公允地评估英国国民医疗服务体系（NHS）与 DeepMind 之间这项协议所含风险的做法，都必须首先承认双方的本意是好的。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants.
sentences.core: The potential ... is very great, but it could also lead to ... .
sentences.structure: applied to healthcare 是过去分词短语，修饰 this work；it 指把 DeepMind 的技术工作应用于医疗这一做法；in the tech giants 表示权力集中在科技巨头手中。
sentences.key: potential：此处作名词，意为“潜力、可能产生的价值”。；concentration of power：权力集中，不是注意力集中。
sentences.zh: 把这项工作应用于医疗保健的潜力十分巨大，但它也可能使权力进一步集中到科技巨头手中。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients’ rights and their expectations of privacy.
sentences.core: It is against that background that the information commissioner has issued her verdict against the hospital trust.
sentences.structure: It is ... that ... 是强调句，突出裁定产生的背景；Elizabeth Denham 是 the information commissioner 的同位语；which handed over ... 是非限制性定语从句，补充说明医院信托做了什么；第二个 which took ... account of ... 修饰 a vague agreement。
sentences.key: trust：常见义为“信任”；此处指 NHS 体系中负责运营医疗机构的“医疗信托机构”。；damning：严厉谴责的、极具否定性的。；take account of：考虑、顾及。；issue a verdict against ...：作出不利于……的裁定。
sentences.zh: 正是在这一背景下，信息专员伊丽莎白·德纳姆对 NHS 旗下的皇家自由医院信托作出了措辞严厉的裁定：该信托在 2015 年依据一份含糊的协议，将 160 万名患者的记录交给 DeepMind，而这份协议远远没有充分顾及患者的权利及其对隐私的合理期待。
sentences.tip: 离第二个 which 最近的先行词是 a vague agreement，因此是协议未充分顾及患者权利，而不是 160 万份患者记录“未顾及权利”。

sentences.en: Further arrangements – and there may be many – between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned.
sentences.core: Further arrangements will be carefully scrutinised.
sentences.structure: 破折号之间是插入语，补充后续安排可能很多；between the NHS and DeepMind 修饰 arrangements；to ensure that ... 表目的；that 从句中两个现在完成时的被动结构并列。
sentences.key: scrutinise：仔细审查；本文采用英式拼写 scrutinised。；clean data：此处结合 unnecessary data，指把不必要的数据清除出数据集，而不是日常意义上的“清洗污渍”。
sentences.zh: NHS 与 DeepMind 之间后续的合作安排——而且可能会有很多——都将受到仔细审查，以确保已经向患者征得所有必要许可，并且已经清除全部非必要数据。
sentences.tip: permissions have been asked of patients 意为“已向患者请求许可”；不是让“许可”去询问患者。

sentences.en: But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important.
sentences.core: Privacy is not the only angle and not even the most important.
sentences.structure: 见原句
sentences.key: angle：常见义为“角度”；此处指分析问题的“方面、视角”。
sentences.zh: 但是，隐私并不是看待本案的唯一角度，甚至不是最重要的角度。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it “controlled” the data and DeepMind merely “processed” it.
sentences.core: Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust.
sentences.structure: since ... 引导原因状语从句；从句内 it “controlled” ... 与 DeepMind merely “processed” ... 并列；第一个 it 指 the NHS trust，第二个 it 指 the data。
sentences.key: concentrate the blame on：把责任主要归到……身上。；under existing law：按照现行法律。
sentences.zh: 德纳姆女士选择把责任集中归于 NHS 医疗信托，因为按照现行法律，是该信托“控制”数据，而 DeepMind 只是“处理”数据。
sentences.tip: 引号标出法律上的角色区分，作者下一句正要质疑这种区分是否抓住问题实质。

sentences.en: But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value.
sentences.core: This distinction misses the point.
sentences.structure: that ... 是 the point 的同位语从句；从句内部是 it is A, not B, that ... 强调句，强调 processing and aggregation 而排除 the mere possession of bits；作者把“处理与聚合”视作一个整体的数据增值过程，因此关系分句使用单数 gives。
sentences.key: miss the point：没有抓住要点、偏离问题实质。；aggregation：聚合、汇总，即把大量分散数据结合起来分析。；bits：此处指零散的数据片段，不宜只译成计算机中的“比特”。
sentences.zh: 但这种区分没有抓住关键：真正赋予数据价值的是对数据的处理与汇总，而不是仅仅占有一个个数据片段。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate.
sentences.core: The great question is who should benefit from the analysis.
sentences.structure: who ... 引导表语从句；of all the data 修饰 analysis；that our lives now generate 是定语从句，修饰 data。
sentences.key: benefit from：从……中获益。；generate data：产生数据。
sentences.zh: 真正重大的问题是：谁应当从对我们如今生活所产生的全部数据的分析中获益。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them.
sentences.core: Privacy law builds on the concept of damage.
sentences.structure: to an individual 说明损害的承受者；from identifiable knowledge about them 说明损害的来源；them 是性别中性的单数代词，回指 an individual。
sentences.key: build on：以……为基础、建立在……之上。；identifiable knowledge：能够识别出特定个人的信息。
sentences.zh: 隐私法建立在这样一种损害概念之上：可识别个人身份的信息会对该个人造成伤害。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more.
sentences.core: The data of an individual gains its value.
sentences.structure: there 指在 the surveillance economy 中；only when ... 表示必要条件，其中 it 指个人数据；countless millions more 指另外数以千万计的人，the data of 在语义上承接前文。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 在监控经济中，一个人的数据只有与另外数以千万计的人的数据进行比较时，才会获得价值。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives.
sentences.core: It is not enough to say ... .
sentences.structure: It 是形式主语，真正主语是 to say ...；that ... 是 say 的宾语从句；DeepMind develops 是省略关系代词的定语从句，修饰 the algorithms。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 仅仅声称 DeepMind 开发的算法将使患者受益并挽救生命，是不够的。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources.
sentences.core: What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly.
sentences.structure: What matters 是主语从句，意为“真正重要的事情”；that ... 是表语从句；they 指前句的 algorithms；which developed them ... 是定语从句，修饰 a private monopoly；using public resources 作方式状语。
sentences.key: private monopoly：私人垄断者或私人垄断企业；此处具体指可能独占算法和数据价值的科技巨头。；public resources：公共资源，这里包括 NHS 的公共医疗体系及患者数据。
sentences.zh: 真正要紧的是，这些算法将归一个私人垄断者所有，而该垄断者是利用公共资源开发出它们的。
sentences.tip: 作者真正担忧的不是算法未经控制地被使用，而是科技巨头利用公共资源开发算法后形成私人垄断。

sentences.en: If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as a big pharma has done.
sentences.core: If software promises ..., big data may be expected to behave ... .
sentences.structure: If ... 引导条件状语从句；on the scale 表示“以这样的规模”；that drugs now can 是定语从句，修饰 the scale，can 后省略 save lives；as ... has done 是方式比较从句，done 代替 behaved。
sentences.key: promise to do sth.：此处不是“承诺做某事”，而是“有望、显示出做某事的潜力”。；big pharma：大型制药企业或制药巨头。
sentences.zh: 如果软件有望像如今的药物那样大规模挽救生命，那么人们也可以预料，大数据企业会像大型制药公司过去那样行事。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later.
sentences.core: We are at the beginning ... and small choices may turn out to have consequences.
sentences.structure: 见原句
sentences.key: at the beginning of：处于……的开端。；turn out to do sth.：结果是……、后来证明会……。；gigantic consequences：极其重大的后果。
sentences.zh: 我们仍处在这场革命的开端，而今天看似微小的选择，日后可能会产生极其重大的后果。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism.
sentences.core: A long struggle will be needed.
sentences.structure: to avoid ... 是目的状语；a future of digital feudalism 指数字资源与权力高度集中于私人垄断者的未来。
sentences.key: digital feudalism：数字封建主义，比喻少数科技巨头像封建领主一样控制关键数据、算法和由此产生的利益。
sentences.zh: 要避免一个数字封建主义的未来，还需要进行长期斗争。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: It reported a net loss of $5.6 billion for fiscal 2016, the 10th straight year its expenses have exceeded revenue.
sentences.core: It reported a net loss.
sentences.structure: of $5.6 billion 说明亏损金额；for fiscal 2016 说明财年；逗号后的名词短语 the 10th straight year ... 补充解释这一亏损的连续性，其中 its expenses have exceeded revenue 是省略关系词的定语从句，修饰 year。
sentences.key: net loss：净亏损。；fiscal 2016：2016 财年。；the 10th straight year：连续第十年。；expenses exceed revenue：支出超过收入。
sentences.zh: 美国邮政署报告称，2016 财年的净亏损为 56 亿美元；这已是其支出连续第十年超过收入。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: There are many reasons this formerly stable federal institution finds itself at the brink of bankruptcy.
sentences.core: There are many reasons.
sentences.structure: (why) this ... institution finds itself ... 是修饰 reasons 的定语从句，省略了关系副词 why；formerly stable 与眼下濒临破产形成对比。
sentences.key: find oneself at the brink of：发现自己处在……的边缘。；at the brink of bankruptcy：濒临破产。
sentences.zh: 这个曾经稳定的联邦机构如今发现自己濒临破产，背后存在许多原因。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its bread-and-butter product, first-class mail, and a regulatory structure that denies management the flexibility to adjust its operations to the new reality.
sentences.core: The USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change and a regulatory structure.
sentences.structure: between A and B 给出困境的两端；that has ... decreased demand ... 修饰 technological change；first-class mail 是 its bread-and-butter product 的同位语；第二个 that ... 修饰 a regulatory structure；to adjust ... 修饰 flexibility。
sentences.key: squeeze：此处作名词，意为“两面夹击、进退两难的困境”。；bread-and-butter：字面为“面包和黄油”；作定语指赖以生存的、最基本的收入来源。；first-class mail：美国邮政的一类邮件，通常包括信件和明信片，不是“头等舱邮件”。；decrease demand for：降低对……的需求。
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，美国邮政署陷入了前所未有的两面夹击：一边是技术变革永久性地削弱了对其支柱产品——一类邮件——的需求；另一边是监管结构不允许管理层灵活调整运营以适应新的现实。
sentences.tip: 原文不是说技术升级成本太高，而是技术变化降低了传统邮件需求；也不是说管理者主观拒绝改革，而是监管结构使管理失去灵活性。

sentences.en: And interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers exert self-interested pressure on the USPS’s ultimate overseer – Congress – insisting that whatever else happens to the Postal Service, aspects of the status quo they depend on get protected.
sentences.core: Interest groups exert pressure on the USPS’s ultimate overseer.
sentences.structure: ranging from ... to ... 修饰 interest groups；破折号之间的 Congress 是 ultimate overseer 的同位语；insisting that ... 是现在分词短语，说明施压时提出的要求；whatever else happens to ... 是让步状语从句；they depend on 是省略关系词的定语从句，修饰 aspects of the status quo。
sentences.key: interest group：利益集团，即围绕共同利益影响公共决策的组织，不是“兴趣小组”。；self-interested：以自身利益为出发点的、自利的。；status quo：现状、既有安排。；range from A to B：范围从 A 延伸到 B。
sentences.zh: 而从邮政工会到贺卡制造商，各类利益集团都出于自身利益向美国邮政署的最高监督者——国会——施压，坚持认为无论邮政系统还会发生什么变化，它们所依赖的那些现状都必须受到保护。
sentences.tip: they 指利益集团；利益集团要求保护的是各自依赖的既有制度安排，而不是笼统保护 USPS。

sentences.en: This is why repeated attempts at reform legislation have failed in recent years, leaving the Postal Service unable to pay its bills except by deferring vital modernization.
sentences.core: This is why repeated attempts ... have failed.
sentences.structure: why ... 引导表语从句；at reform legislation 修饰 attempts；leaving ... 是现在分词短语，表示改革失败造成的结果；unable to pay ... 作宾补；except by deferring ... 表示唯一勉强应对财务压力的办法。
sentences.key: pay one’s bills：支付应付款项、维持财务偿付，不仅指日常缴费。；defer：推迟、延后。
sentences.zh: 这正是近年来一次次邮政改革立法尝试均告失败的原因，结果美国邮政署除了推迟至关重要的现代化改造之外，已无力支付各项账单。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Now comes word that everyone involved – Democrats, Republicans, the Postal Service, the unions and the system’s heaviest users – has finally agreed on a plan to fix the system.
sentences.core: Now comes word.
sentences.structure: Now 前置引起完全倒装，正常语序为 Word now comes；that ... 是 word 的同位语从句；破折号之间列举 everyone involved 所包含的各方；to fix the system 修饰 a plan。
sentences.key: word：常见义为“单词”；此处作不可数名词，意为“消息”。；heavy user：某项服务的高频或大量使用者，不是“体重较大的用户”。
sentences.zh: 如今传来消息：所有相关方——民主党人、共和党人、美国邮政署、工会以及邮政系统的最大用户——终于就一项修复该系统的方案达成了一致。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Legislation is moving through the House that would save USPS an estimated $28.6 billion over five years, which could help pay for new vehicles, among other survival measures.
sentences.core: Legislation is moving through the House.
sentences.structure: that would save ... 是定语从句，修饰 Legislation；an estimated $28.6 billion 作 save 的直接宾语，USPS 是间接宾语；which could help pay ... 承接前述节省下来的资金及其作用；among other survival measures 表示购置车辆只是多项求生措施之一。
sentences.key: the House：美国国会众议院。；move through：此处指法案在立法程序中推进。；survival measures：帮助机构维持运转、渡过危机的措施。
sentences.zh: 一项法案正在众议院推进，预计可在五年内为美国邮政署节省 286 亿美元；除其他维持生存的措施外，这笔钱还可以帮助购买新车辆。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Most of the money would come from a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase and from shifting postal retirees into Medicare.
sentences.core: Most of the money would come from A and from B.
sentences.structure: 两个 from 引出并列资金来源；A 是复合定语很长的名词短语，B 是 shifting ... 动名词短语。
sentences.key: a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase：每封信永久加价一美分。；shift sb. into Medicare：把某人转入美国联邦医疗保险计划。；postal retirees：邮政系统退休人员。
sentences.zh: 大部分资金将来自两项措施：永久性地将每封信的邮资提高一美分，以及把邮政退休人员纳入联邦医疗保险计划。
sentences.tip: money 并非全部用于购车；本句在解释法案如何节省资金和减轻负担。

sentences.en: The latter step would largely offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care, thus addressing a long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions.
sentences.core: The latter step would offset the financial burden.
sentences.structure: of annually pre-funding ... 修饰 burden，说明负担来自何处；thus addressing ... 是现在分词短语，表示由减轻负担自然产生的结果。
sentences.key: the latter step：指前句两项措施中的后一项，即把邮政退休人员纳入 Medicare。；offset：抵消、弥补。；pre-fund：预先筹资，在费用实际发生前先行备足资金。；address a complaint：处理、回应一项不满或诉求。
sentences.zh: 后一项措施将大幅抵消每年预先为退休人员医疗保障筹资所造成的财务负担，从而回应美国邮政署及其工会长期以来的一项不满。
sentences.tip: 解决长期不满的是转入 Medicare 后减轻退休人员医疗预筹资负担，不是购买新车或单纯提高邮资。

sentences.en: If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate – where someone is bound to point out that it amounts to the bare, bare minimum necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, not comprehensive reform.
sentences.core: If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate.
sentences.structure: it 指 this measure；破折号后的 where ... 是非限制性定语从句，修饰 the Senate；is bound to 表示必然；that ... 是 point out 的宾语从句；necessary to keep ... 修饰 the bare, bare minimum；句尾 not comprehensive reform 与最低限度措施形成否定对照。
sentences.key: clear the House：获众议院通过，不是“清空众议院”。；get through the Senate：通过参议院审议。；amount to：等同于、实质上是。；keep ... afloat：本义为使……漂浮；此处指使机构在财务上维持运转、不致倒闭。
sentences.zh: 即便该措施在众议院获得通过，它仍须过参议院这一关——在那里必定会有人指出，它不过是维持美国邮政署生存所必需的最低限度措施，远非全面改革。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: There’s no change to collective bargaining at the USPS, a major omission considering that personnel accounts for 80 percent of the agency’s costs.
sentences.core: There’s no change to collective bargaining.
sentences.structure: a major omission 是对前面整个事实的同位补充和评价；considering that ... 表示作出这一评价的依据，其中 that ... 是 considering 的宾语从句。
sentences.key: collective bargaining：集体谈判，通常指工会代表员工与雇主协商工资和劳动条件。；personnel：此处不是单指“人事部门”，而是指人员及相关成本。；account for：占据某一比例。
sentences.zh: 该方案没有改变美国邮政署的集体谈判制度；考虑到人员成本占该机构总成本的 80%，这是一个重大遗漏。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Also missing is any discussion of eliminating Saturday letter delivery.
sentences.core: Any discussion ... is also missing.
sentences.structure: 表语 Also missing 前置引起完全倒装；of eliminating ... 修饰 discussion。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 同样缺失的，还有关于取消周六信件投递的任何讨论。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: That common-sense change enjoys wide public support and would save the USPS $2 billion per year.
sentences.core: That change enjoys support and would save the USPS $2 billion.
sentences.structure: 两个谓语 enjoys 与 would save 并列；save sb. money 是双宾语结构；That ... change 回指取消周六信件投递。
sentences.key: common-sense：合乎常理的、务实明智的；该评价直接体现作者支持取消周六信件投递。
sentences.zh: 这一符合常理的改革得到公众广泛支持，而且每年可为美国邮政署节省 20 亿美元。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: But postal special-interest groups seem to have killed it, at least in the House.
sentences.core: Postal special-interest groups seem to have killed it.
sentences.structure: seem to have done 表示看来某事已经发生；it 指前文取消周六信件投递的改革；at least in the House 限定该改革在众议院阶段遭到阻止。
sentences.key: kill a proposal/change：扼杀、阻止一项提案或改革获得通过。；special-interest group：特殊利益集团，指为特定群体利益影响决策的组织。
sentences.zh: 但是，邮政特殊利益集团似乎已经扼杀了这项改革，至少在众议院是如此。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: The emerging consensus around the bill is a sign that legislators are getting frightened about a politically embarrassing short-term collapse at the USPS.
sentences.core: The emerging consensus is a sign.
sentences.structure: around the bill 修饰 consensus；that ... 是 a sign 的同位语从句；about ... collapse 说明立法者害怕的事情；politically embarrassing 修饰 collapse，实际强调崩溃会给立法者造成政治后果。
sentences.key: emerging consensus：正在形成的共识。；politically embarrassing：会造成政治难堪的、在政治上有损颜面的。
sentences.zh: 围绕这项法案逐渐形成的共识表明，立法者开始害怕美国邮政署在短期内崩溃，因为那会令他们在政治上难堪。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: It is not, however, a sign that they’re getting serious about transforming the postal system for the 21stcentury.
sentences.core: It is not a sign.
sentences.structure: however 是插入的转折副词；that ... 是 a sign 的同位语从句；about transforming ... 是 get serious 的介词宾语；for the 21st century 说明转型应适应新时代需要。
sentences.key: get serious about：开始认真对待、真正着手处理。；It：指上一句所说的“围绕法案形成共识”这一事实。；they：指 legislators（立法者）。；bleed red ink：持续出现赤字、不断亏损。
sentences.zh: 然而，这并不表明他们开始认真推动邮政系统转型，以适应 21 世纪。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。
